To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cell surface of myocytes from the hypertrophied aging hearts of the spontaneously hypertensive rat has increased cell junction areas and capillary grooves.
The surface morphology of isolated cardiac cells from hypertrophied rat hearts was characterized by increased surface area and cell junction areas.

the cell surface of cardiac myocytes obtained by collagenase perfusion of hearts from 12 and, especially, 48-week old spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) has deep capillary groves which are surrounded by protruding bundles of myof fibrils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of chronic hypertension on the structure and function of the heart and its blood vessels.
the study of the morphologic and functional changes which occur in the hearts of spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) with aging and hypertension.
the study of cardiac cell morphology and its relationship to the development of cardiac hypertrophy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

hypertrophy of the SHR heart is associated with increased numbers of cell surface areas which are involved in the transfer of substances from the capillaries to the tissue and from the tissue to the blood.
these results are not consistent with the hypothesis that increased surface area of cardiac myocytes is a compensatory mechanism in the hypertrophically enlarged heart.
the morphological alterations of the myocyte in the SHR are adaptive changes which may serve as a compensatory mechanism to the increased metabolic demands placed on the hypertrophied heart.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypertrophied hearts in SHR are able to adapt to increased workload by increasing the surface to volume ratio of the cardiac myocytes.
the hypertrophied heart of the SHR undergoes a compensatory response in the form of increased cell size, increased surface area of cells, and increased capillary density.
the hypertrophy is a compensatory process which is not deleterious to cardiac function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hypertrophied cardiac myocytes from aging hypertensive animals have a unique surface morphology which may have a protective effect against ischemia and infarction.
the surface area to volume ratio of the cell is maintained at an optimal level by hypertrophy of the cell.
the surface morphology of the myocyte changes as the heart hypertrophies and these changes may have a protective effect.
